text:
emily: heads up — after the HF->Redwood conversion a couple of our evals started failing. small repro attached, looks like a control token id got shadowed by an added_tokens entry. cc @raj @maria

raj: yikes. which token? pad/bos/eos/unk? any quick dump?

emily: minimal dump below. i loaded the hf tokenizer, then printed ids for control symbols and first few added_tokens.
```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('our-hf-fork')
print('bos', t.convert_tokens_to_ids([t.bos_token]))
print('eos', t.convert_tokens_to_ids([t.eos_token]))
print('pad', t.convert_tokens_to_ids([t.pad_token]))
print('unk', t.convert_tokens_to_ids([t.unk_token]))
print('first_added', [t.convert_tokens_to_ids([x])[0] for x in t.backend_tokenizer.get_added_tokens().keys()][:6])
```
logs:
```
bos [2]
eos [3]
pad [1]
unk [0]
first_added [2, 57, 58, 59, 60, 61]
```

emily: notice first_added[0] == 2 which is bos. that means the string in added_tokens.json serialized to a token that already maps to bos. downstream Redwood importer then remapped ids and shifted the whole vocab, breaking chat templates that expect fixed ids.

maria: interesting — is the added token literally the same string as bos token or is it a substring/normalization artifact? hf tokenizers sometimes normalize unicode and combine control symbols.

emily: checked added_tokens.json — there was an entry "<s>" (the same as bos) that was mistakenly included by a script that merges community added tokens. but the HF tokenizer had both a special token and an added_tokens entry for the same string, which made the tokenizer assign the existing special id to the added token index and also keep an added_tokens slot referencing that id. the end result during our conversion: index collisions + downstream id remapping.

raj: ah. so two pathways created the same string: special_tokens_map and added_tokens.json. HF's tokenizer allowed it, but Redwood import expects these to be disjoint.

maria: can you paste the offending snippet from added_tokens.json? also which conversion step are we running (hf->tokenizer.json -> redwood-vocab)?

emily: snippet:
```
["<s>", "<|system|>", "<|user|>", "<|assistant|>", "<pad_custom>"]
```
conversion: we call our import script that wraps tokenizers.TokenizerFast.save_pretrained() then run redwood_importer --input tokenizer.json --added added_tokens.json --out redwood_vocab.bin

raj: short term mitigation: filter added_tokens.json against the special_tokens_map before running import. if token string equals any special token, drop it. also run t.encode(special) and ensure ids do not collide.

maria: medium-term: make the importer stricter — error out if any added token string normalizes equal to an existing special token or if convert_tokens_to_ids returns an id that matches a control token. add a check that added_tokens indices are all > max_special_id.

emily: agreed. for immediate unblock i patched the merge script to dedupe and re-ran the import. the canary evals passed. will open a PR with a unit test that simulates this.

raj: thanks. can you also add a quick verification in the onboarding checklist: run `python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; print({ 'bos':t.bos_token, 'added': list(t.backend_tokenizer.get_added_tokens().keys())[:5] })"` and make sure no overlap? small script is fine.

emily: yep will add. also adding a check in our quant import path — quantization reorders indices in some internal formats and we should assert control tokens stay fixed.

deploy-bot: conversion-job-3721 finished with status SUCCESS (patched importer).

maria: perfect. follow-up: we should add a short note in docs about special_tokens vs added_tokens and normalization pitfalls (unicode, nbsp, zero-width). i can draft.

emily: thanks — i'll include the snippet and the failing log lines in the PR. :thumbsup:
